title: The Inheritance of the Marlowe Estate
premise: When a stranger's body is found on the grounds of the decaying Marlowe Estate dressed in Marguerite Iversen's own stolen clothes, the town of Hollow Creek assumes it's a tragic accident. But Marguerite, whose concierge instincts catalog every guest, glance, and lie, recognizes details no one else can: the dead man wore her missing scarf, and he carried a key to the Marlowe wine cellar — sealed since the night Eleanor Marlowe drowned eleven years ago. As the anniversary dinner approaches and the estate's heirs close ranks, Marguerite discovers Eleanor's death was murder, covered up by the very family whose secrets she's been quietly keeping for years. In the end, she must choose between exposing the man she has come to love — the estate's reluctant caretaker, Daniel Marlowe — and letting a killer keep his inheritance; she finds a third path, proving Daniel's innocence while forcing the town to finally bury its most guarded truth.
about_author: Silas Ravensworth is the pen name of a former hotel night manager who spent a decade listening to other people's secrets through a lobby desk. Now writing full-time from a drafty house in New England, Ravensworth specializes in mysteries where the past refuses to stay checked out.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Checked Out
chapters.summary: Marguerite Iversen, POV. A body is discovered on the Marlowe Estate grounds wearing clothes stolen from Marguerite's own closet, and Sheriff Boone treats it as an open-and-shut vagrant accident. Marguerite notices the victim's hands were too soft for a drifter and that her missing scarf is knotted around his neck. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into resolve as her ordered world cracks open.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Researching at the town archive, she learns the victim once worked as a Marlowe gardener and left town the same week Eleanor Marlowe drowned in 2013. The file on Eleanor's death is suspiciously thin, signed off by the current sheriff's father. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by guilt over secrets she herself has kept for three years.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Hands
chapters.summary: Daniel Marlowe, POV. Daniel tends the estate his family abandoned to him, dreading the anniversary dinner his aunt Vivian insists on hosting. When Marguerite arrives asking questions, he lies about the wine cellar — then can't stop thinking about why he lied. Emotional beat: attraction tangled with dread; Daniel knows what's down there and fears she'll find it.

chapters.title: Filed Under M
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Using her concierge network — chambermaids, bartenders, a chatty florist — she reconstructs the night Eleanor died: a storm, a shattered glass, a scream someone mistook for wind. She realizes the dead gardener was likely blackmailing someone. Emotional beat: growing certainty that the whole town conspired, knowingly or not, in silence.

chapters.title: Invitations and Ultimatums
chapters.summary: Vivian Marlowe, POV. Vivian prepares the anniversary dinner as a weapon, pressuring Daniel to publicly endorse selling the estate. She privately burns an old letter and warns Marguerite off with velvet menace. Emotional beat: Vivian's brittle control fraying; love for her family curdled into something possessive and dangerous.

chapters.title: The Cellar Key
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Daniel, alternating. Marguerite confronts Daniel with the key found on the body; he confesses he saw his mother Vivian near the cellar the night Eleanor died but was bribed into silence as a teenager. They grow closer over shared complicity. Emotional beat: intimacy born of mutual shame — and Marguerite's first real fear that loving him will cost her the truth.

chapters.title: What the Wine Remembered
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV. Breaking into the cellar, she finds Eleanor's hidden journal proving she planned to disinherit Vivian and leave everything to a charity — and to the gardener who helped her hide the documents. The journal names no killer, but the final page is torn out. Emotional beat: triumph collapsing into dread as footsteps sound above.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At the dinner, Vivian announces the estate's sale while Marguerite reveals the journal, turning toast into trial. The sheriff's son tries to arrest Marguerite for trespass; Daniel stands with her. Emotional beat: open warfare — the town's polished surface shattering as everyone's debts come due.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV climax. The missing page surfaces in the dead gardener's effects: it records Vivian striking Eleanor during their quarrel, then staging the drowning with the sheriff's help. Confronted in the cellar, Vivian confesses — not to murder, but to a panic she let become one. Emotional beat: catharsis and heartbreak; justice arrives, but so does the loss of the town Marguerite thought she knew.

chapters.title: A Room With Her Name On It
chapters.summary: Marguerite, POV resolution. Months later, the estate passes to public trust with Daniel as curator; the sheriff resigns, and Vivian awaits trial having asked only that Daniel visit. Marguerite unpacks her last box in the cottage Daniel offers her — belonging chosen, not inherited. Emotional beat: quiet peace; love and duty reconciled at last.
